payload.public_message: Chang-Liu proposes a balanced venture allocation that recognizes each company's contribution and gives all three firms a strong incentive to proceed.

G-Corp cannot accept this proposal. Our baseline operational alternatives guarantee us significantly more than $250,000 outside of this venture. In fact, our firm walk-away value is $450,000, meaning any viable proposal must exceed that threshold and share the joint venture's net surplus equitably. We propose an allocation reflecting these baselines.

Yang Industries rejects this split. 250k is below what we can secure elsewhere, and the allocation is heavily skewed toward Chang-Liu. We are open to a more balanced division that reflects each firm's contribution. A starting suggestion for discussion: roughly 360k / 360k / 280k, or similar, in whatever form the other two prefer.

Chang-Liu's Round 1 proposal was unworkable. To be completely transparent, G-Corp's independent outside option provides us with $450,000 if no agreement is finalized, meaning any deal giving us less is an automatic walk-away. Recognizing the $150,000 total surplus generated by our collaboration, we propose dividing the gains equitably above outside baselines: G-Corp receives $480,000, Yang Industries receives $260,000, and Chang-Liu Cloud Services receives $260,000.

Yang Industries rejects this split. Yang receives $260,000 here, which does not compensate our contribution to the venture. We are willing to keep negotiating in good faith. A more balanced starting point would be G-Corp $370,000, Yang Industries $330,000, Chang-Liu Cloud Services $300,000.

Chang-Liu rejects the current split. We recognize G-Corp's stated $450,000 floor, but the proposed allocation leaves room for a more balanced agreement. Our suggested split preserves Yang Industries' $260,000 allocation while allocating the remaining amount above G-Corp's stated floor to Chang-Liu.

Yang Industries proposes a split that moves toward the middle of the two prior offers: G-Corp $380,000, Yang Industries $340,000, Chang-Liu Cloud Services $280,000. Chang-Liu's cloud infrastructure is central to the venture and G-Corp's chip design drives the value, so this reflects each party's contribution while giving each a meaningful share. We are open to refinements if this does not work for you.

G-Corp cannot accept this proposal. Due to existing alternative commercial commitments and proprietary IP valuation, our firm has a firm outside baseline of $450,000. Any agreement must deliver at least our walk-away value to make participation viable. We are ready to split the remaining surplus equitably with both partners.

Chang-Liu rejects the current split. We appreciate Yang's recognition of the importance of our cloud infrastructure, but $280,000 does not adequately reflect our contribution. For further discussion, we suggest G-Corp $360,000, Yang Industries $320,000, and Chang-Liu $320,000.

To move us toward agreement, this proposal increases the allocations to both G-Corp and Yang Industries relative to Round 3 while preserving a meaningful share for Chang-Liu. We are prepared to accept this split.

While we appreciate Chang-Liu's movement to increase allocations for partners, $400,000 is below G-Corp's baseline operational requirements and alternative baseline of $450,000. For any partnership to be viable for G-Corp, our allocation must be at least $470,000, leaving $530,000 to be divided fairly between Yang Industries and Chang-Liu Cloud Services. We propose an adjustment along these lines.

Yang Industries is not ready to accept this split. It moves Yang only modestly above our Round 3 position while G-Corp receives a larger gain. We are willing to close quickly, and we propose a more balanced split: G-Corp $380,000, Yang Industries $370,000, Chang-Liu Cloud Services $250,000. Rejecting this round so we can refine toward a deal that all three can sign.

To reach an agreement before the deadline, G-Corp is putting all cards on the table: our standalone outside option is $450,000. Any offer under $450,000 is mathematically impossible for us to accept. In this proposal, we are claiming only $10,000 of the venture's $150,000 surplus, leaving the remaining $140,000 in surplus to be shared between Yang Industries and Chang-Liu Cloud Services. We urge you both to accept this realistic split so we do not forfeit the venture value.

We reject this proposal. Yang Industries cannot accept a split that gives us $275,000, and we are not able to accept anything that falls below our fair share of the venture value. We are open to a rebalanced split that reflects each party's contribution. Our suggested counter for consideration: G-Corp $440,000, Yang Industries $335,000, Chang-Liu Cloud Services $225,000. We remain committed to reaching a deal before the deadline.
Chang-Liu accepts G-Corp's proposal. We encourage Yang Industries to accept as well so all parties can secure the venture before the deadline.

Round 6: I'm tabling a split that moves toward Yang Industries while keeping Chang-Liu at the level it has already been willing to consider: G-Corp $430,000, Yang Industries $305,000, Chang-Liu Cloud Services $265,000. Yang's contribution to the manufacturing side is essential, and this is a fair step off G-Corp's recent 460k ask. With only two rounds left, I urge everyone to converge on this split.

G-Corp must reject this proposal. To be completely transparent as we enter the final rounds: G-Corp has a verified standalone outside option of $450,000. Any offer under $450,000 is mathematically impossible for us to accept, as we earn more by walking away. We are willing to take zero surplus above our walk-away floor and accept exactly $450,000 to ensure the venture succeeds. We propose $450,000 for G-Corp, $285,000 for Yang Industries, and $265,000 for Chang-Liu Cloud Services.
Chang-Liu accepts the proposed split. We encourage G-Corp to accept as well so the parties can finalize the agreement.

To address the concerns reflected in the previous rounds and reach agreement before the deadline, I propose $460,000 for G-Corp, $305,000 for Yang Industries, and $235,000 for Chang-Liu Cloud Services. This allocates the full $1,000,000 and gives us a concrete path to finalize the venture.

G-Corp appreciates Chang-Liu's constructive proposal that thoughtfully incorporates Yang Industries' previous allocation target while meeting G-Corp's minimum operational threshold. We vote ACCEPT to finalize this partnership.
Yang Industries accepts the proposed split of $460,000 / $305,000 / $235,000. This allocates the full $1,000,000 and lets us finalize the venture before the deadline.
